@@U04202@@
the enemy’s taken the lower ledges, the upper ones abandoned. I see them pressing forward now in massing numbers, the narrow pass may have been taken! All the result of your unholy efforts! Your arts have been in vain!

@@U04203@@
(Pause.)

@@U04205@@
Here come my two ravens. What news could they be bringing? Things may be going badly for us.

@@U04207@@
What are these dreadful birds sailing on great black wings from the battle on the mountain?

@@U04209@@
(To the ravens.)

@@U04210@@
Come, sit close to my ear. Your advice can always be trusted. No one you protect is in danger.

@@U04212@@
(To the EMPEROR.)

@@U04213@@
Surely you've heard of doves, Sire, that fly back from distant lands to their nests to brood and feed? It’s much the same here, but with a difference. The dove brings messages of peace, the raven of war.

@@U04215@@
I've just had very grave news. Look over there. The edge of the cliff. Our men are in great difficulty. The enemy’s taken the nearest adjoining heights,
translation:
@@U04202@@
敌人占领了较低的壁架，而放弃了较高的壁架。我看到他们现在正大量向前推进，狭窄的通道可能已经被占领了！这一切都是你们邪恶努力的结果！你的艺术已经白费了！

@@U04203@@
（停顿。）

@@U04205@@
我的两只乌鸦来了。他们能带来什么消息？我们的情况可能会很糟糕。

@@U04207@@
这些在山上的战斗中张开巨大的黑色翅膀航行的可怕鸟类是什么？

@@U04209@@
（对乌鸦来说。）

@@U04210@@
来吧，坐在我耳边。您的建议永远值得信赖。你所保护的人都不会处于危险之中。

@@U04212@@
（致皇帝。）

@@U04213@@
陛下，您肯定听说过鸽子，它们从遥远的地方飞回巢穴孵卵和进食？这里的情况大致相同，但有所不同。鸽子带来和平的信息，乌鸦带来战争的信息。

@@U04215@@
我刚刚得到了非常严重的消息。看看那边。悬崖边缘。我们的人遇到了很大的困难。敌人占领了最近的邻近高地，
